title: Compress rollout metadata and migrate legacy config shards to canonical store
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: Over years we accumulated many per-release and per-customer rollout artifacts: JSON blobs in S3, versioned admin endpoints, ephemeral rollout IDs, and a handful of synonyms for the same feature toggle. This increases runtime complexity (multiple code paths to read config), slows rollout resolution in the router, and complicates auditing. Goal: replace scattered legacy shards with a single canonical config store (read-optimized table + small service facade), compress/normalize historical rollout metadata into a compact canonical schema, and retire the old config endpoints and per-tenant variants. The migration must preserve rollout semantics, support audits, and be reversible in the short term.
migration_steps: Define canonical schema: rollout_id, canonical_key, target_rules (condensed), created_at, last_modified_by, history_blob_ref
Implement canonical-config service with read-only facade for initial migration (no live writes)
Build a batch compressor that reads legacy blobs and emits normalized canonical records with mapping table (legacy_id -> canonical_id)
Run dry-run on staging using a snapshot of production metadata; validate equivalence with a selector-based comparator
Apply online migration: create canonical records in prod in small batches (rate-limited), publish mapping, and run canary queries against router and console
Flip runtime read path to prefer canonical-config service with a short TTL fallback to legacy endpoints for 72 hours
Monitor telemetry; once stable, stop reading from legacy endpoints and mark them deprecated
Schedule removal of legacy endpoints and S3 blobs after retention window and audit completion
testing_plan: Unit tests for compressor and canonical schema validation
Integration tests: router + canonical-config service returning identical resolution for 1000 sampled rollout inputs
Staging full dry-run with comparator report (match rate >= 99.99%)
Load test canonical-config service at 2x peak read QPS
End-to-end smoke tests for Console rollout pages and rollback workflows
Security scan for migration tool and new service (dependency check + SCA)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): run compressor against snapshot and validate
Phase 1 (canary): migrate 1% of production keys and route 5% of runtime traffic to canonical read path
Phase 2 (ramp): increase to 25%/50% with continuous validation and health gates
Phase 3 (cutover): prefer canonical reads with legacy fallback for 72 hours
Phase 4 (retire): disable legacy endpoints and begin archival after audit window
rollback_plan: If comparator mismatch > 0.01% or runtime error rate increases by > 0.5% vs baseline, revert runtime to legacy read path, pause migration, and run targeted investigations. Mapping table inserts are idempotent: we will mark canonical records with a 'migrated_at' and rely on immutable history_blob_ref to restore previous state if needed.
notes: 2026-02-25: Initial design doc posted; suggested compression format is protobuf with gzip based on size tests
2026-03-01: Schema review flagged high-cardinality rule conditions; changed to reference small predicate table instead of inlining
2026-03-05: Compressor prototype ran against 30k historical blobs and reduced total footprint by 68%
2026-03-09: Opened PR for canonical-config service; needs infra sign-off for DB read-replicas
2026-03-11: Decided to prefer read-prefer canonical with TTL fallback vs dual-write to minimize write-side risk
Next steps: get DB migration window approved, finish comparator automation, schedule staging dry-run
